title: Organizing: a method for organising the class
summary: From mobilisation to building collective power.
body:
Course themes

  • Advocacy, mobilising and organising
  • Organic leaders and the whole worker
  • Mapping and structure tests
  • Power analysis and campaign design
  • Tenant unionism and rent strikes

What will we work on?

Practising organising tools that can be applied to a housing block, a workplace or a collective conflict.

Context and approach

The course starts from Jane McAlevey’s method and her distinction between advocacy, mobilising and organising. The aim is to study how majorities are built among the people affected and how the workplace and the community are brought together.

These tools will be put in dialogue with the experience of tenant unionism: organising a block, taking action against a common landlord and preparing collective bargaining. Practical work will include role-played conversations, mapping, power analysis and designing a campaign.
introduction: Filling a demonstration is not the same as having the power to win a conflict. We will work on tools to talk with people, identify leaders, measure strength and prepare campaigns.
